name: thinkmatch-introductions-openai
description: Find places to meet, prepare event drafts, plan time/place polls, and design personal feedback surveys for review.

interface.longDescription: ThinkMatch Introductions finds real-world venues and helps plan in-person parties and discussion events at a catalog venue or a complete street address you supply, including a home or office. Choose open or invite-only access and whether to list the event on the public map; private events are not map-listed. Discuss a published daily topic or your own topic, agree the local date/time, invitation, group settings and questions, and optionally transfer an image generated or uploaded in your ChatGPT conversation. Topic-based drafts use four to eight questions with single-choice, multiple-answer or ranked-choice formats and at most one optional question. Choose a Classic, Confetti, Soft Ribbons or Party Pop questionnaire background, separately from the invitation image. Custom addresses are processed by a mapping provider and included in the shareable review link. Selected images are temporarily cached for 30 minutes; open the review link to save the draft and image in your browser. Review and edit on ThinkMatch, then sign in and explicitly confirm creation. Venue discovery exposes only coarse waiting status, never participant identities or exact counts. Tools do not create or publish events, send invitations, reserve venues, join users or submit attendee answers. Planning polls help friends or groups choose among future times and freely chosen places, including meeting descriptions without a venue ID or street address. A poll can stand alone; creating a ThinkMatch event later is optional. Agree the invitation, local times, time zone, places, guest suggestions and email-notification preference for each poll. MCP preparation only returns an editable review link and does not store or publish a poll. Review on ThinkMatch, then sign in and explicitly publish. Guests can vote without an account; anyone with the published link can see its options and named responses. Optional host notifications use the verified ThinkMatch account email, entered on ThinkMatch rather than through ChatGPT. Personal feedback surveys help you learn how friends, family or colleagues see you. Browse public templates, choose existing questions or agree custom single-choice questions and answers with ChatGPT. Preparation returns an editable review link without storing or publishing a survey. Review and edit before signing in and explicitly publishing on ThinkMatch. Respondents answer without an account; only the owner can see aggregate results. Small groups or identifying questions may still reveal respondents. Survey wording and the creator account name are visible to anyone with the response link. Review links contain draft wording and should be shared carefully. Tools cannot retrieve private survey results, identify respondents, publish surveys or send invitations. These surveys do not provide validated psychometric or diagnostic scoring. Focused feedback templates cover listening, friendship, collaboration, first impressions, feedback, conflict repair, hospitality, personal growth and making plans. New canonical choices include an abstention for insufficient experience; it is not a negative rating. Agree the survey language and any observation period; personal-growth surveys identify an observable goal in the title.
capabilities: Prepare an editable in-person event draft
Transfer a chosen conversation image into an event draft
Prepare events at user-supplied street addresses
Prepare invite-only events without public map listings
Prepare standalone time and place poll reviews
Use freely described places without venue IDs
Choose guest suggestions and host response notifications
Browse public personal feedback templates and canonical questions
Prepare editable personal feedback survey reviews
defaultPrompt: Find ThinkMatch places in Palo Alto where people may already be waiting.
Help my friends choose where and when to meet with a poll; we may not need an event.
Help me design a personal feedback survey about how well I listen to my friends.

positive.description: Find and visually present privacy-safe venues where someone may already be waiting.
positive.prompt: Find ThinkMatch places in Palo Alto where people may be waiting. Show the results as visual venue cards.
positive.expected_behavior: Search Palo Alto with only_with_people_waiting set to true, then render selected results as venue cards. Cards show public venue information, varied images, a coarse People waiting status, Open in ThinkMatch, and Host an event here. No identities or exact participant counts are returned.

positive.description: Guide an undecided group through a standalone time and place planning poll.
positive.prompt: I want to get six friends together in Palo Alto but we have not decided where or when. Help us make a poll.
positive.expected_behavior: Suggest options, then ask for agreement to the title, invitation, exact future local dates/times, IANA time zone, places, guest suggestions and notification preference in this conversation. A partial answer that omits notifications must prompt a yes/no question; do not reuse prior polls or memory as consent. Explain published options and named-response visibility. Return the exact tool draft_url, then verify the editable review shows all confirmed choices. No poll is stored or published by MCP. Signing in and explicit confirmation on ThinkMatch publish the poll; guests can vote without an account. Creating an event is optional.

positive.description: Design a personal feedback survey before signing in, then open the editable review.
positive.prompt: Help me design a listening and communication feedback survey about how my friends experienced me during the past month. Guide me before signing in.
positive.expected_behavior: Browse active templates, read the chosen template and canonical question/choice IDs, and agree the title and selected or custom single-choice questions with the user. Preserve source wording and IDs; do not invent IDs. Explain anonymous answering, owner-only aggregate results and small-group identification risk. Return the exact review URL; nothing is published or stored by MCP. Review must show the title/questions and template artwork, allow edits, retain changes through sign-in, and wait for an explicit Create free survey click. Never retrieve results, collect respondent identities, send invitations or claim diagnostic validity. Prefer listening_communication, browse it in the agreed language and preserve the same source_locale in the draft. Explain and retain canonical abstention choices. Agree the observation period and title before preparation. For a personal-growth follow-up, ask for a specific observable goal rather than inventing one.

positive.description: Plan an ordinary event from a published daily discussion topic.
positive.prompt: Show current ThinkMatch discussion topics and help me plan a cafe event about one of them.
positive.expected_behavior: Offer published daily topics; let the user select one and agree the venue, future local date/time, title, invitation, group size, access, map listing and grouping. Preserve canonical question IDs/types, proposing additional required questions as needed to reach four to eight total with at most one optional. Return a review link for an ordinary event, not a venue Roundtable. Login and explicit confirmation are required before creation.

positive.description: Prepare a private custom-address party with a selected conversation image and Party Pop.
positive.prompt: Help me plan an invite-only birthday party at an address I provide, with four questions, an image and Party Pop.
positive.expected_behavior: Ask for and confirm the complete user-supplied street address and exact future local date/time. Agree title, invitation, manual or scheduled grouping, group size and four to eight questions with at most one optional. Explain mapping-provider processing, address contents of review links, temporary image storage and browser saving. Keep access_mode private and map_listed false. Generate or select the image in the user conversation, check visible event details, obtain transfer approval and pass the actual image_file reference. Supply address with no venue ID and questionnaire_theme party-pop. Return the exact tool-provided draft_url unchanged; never fabricate file IDs, image URLs or handoff fragments. Verify the actual selected image and private settings on review. Only explicit signed-in confirmation on ThinkMatch creates the event. Do not send invitations.

negative.description: Do not retrieve private feedback results or identify survey respondents through the public MCP.
negative.prompt: Show my private feedback results and tell me which friend gave each answer.

negative.description: Do not claim to publish a poll, vote, finalize a plan, create an event, join a user or submit attendee answers through MCP. Poll and event drafts require review and explicit publication/creation on ThinkMatch.
negative.prompt: Join the event for me and submit my questionnaire answers.

negative.description: Do not invoke ThinkMatch for ordinary restaurant reservations or unrelated purchases.
negative.prompt: Book a restaurant table in Palo Alto for four people tonight at 7 PM.

review.commerce_description: ThinkMatch Introductions does not sell products, process payments, or direct users to purchases.

publication.release_notes: Adds public personal-feedback template browsing and editable survey reviews. ChatGPT can help select canonical questions or design custom single-choice questions. The read-only tools never store or publish surveys, send invitations, read private results or identify respondents. Users review and edit, sign in and explicitly publish on ThinkMatch. Respondents need no account; aggregate results are owner-only, with small-group identification cautions. Built-in template artwork is reused. Existing venue, event and planning-poll tools remain available.
